name: Fish-containing baby food
scope_note: PROVISIONAL SCAFFOLD, grounded entirely by disclosed read-across (no scope-matched direct). Fish-containing baby food carries two naturally elevated, fish-driven analytes: total mercury (bioaccumulated methylmercury) and total arsenic (predominantly non-toxic organic arsenobetaine). Those two cells take aquatic sovereign limits (total-Hg from the EU fish general ML 500; total-As from the Israel seafood ML 1000), while the non-fish hazards (Pb, Cd, iAs, Ni) take strict infant baby-food ceilings, since a fish baby food is still an infant food and those hazards are not fish-elevated. The toxic inorganic-arsenic fraction stays capped at the infant limit (iAs 20 <= tAs 1000). Methylmercury is bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) for now. OPEN / NOT LOCKED: the fish-specific methylmercury read-across (a species-appropriate MeHg ceiling from the Cat-6 Seafood standard) and the infant-protective-vs-fish-realistic basis for the mercury cell await the Cat-6 species-MeHg read-across decision before this scaffold is promoted to a firm standard.

Pb.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2023/915 lead 20 for baby food and processed cereal-based food for infants and young children. Lead is not a fish-elevated hazard, so the strict infant ceiling governs.
Pb.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

Cd.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2023/915 cadmium 40 for baby food and processed cereal-based food for infants and young children.
Cd.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

tAs.label: government read-across (aquatic) — Israel FCS-2016 seafood total-arsenic 1000, reflecting fish's naturally high total arsenic (predominantly non-toxic organic arsenobetaine). The toxic inorganic fraction (iAs) is separately capped at the infant baby-food limit (iAs <= tAs).
tAs.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

iAs.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2023/915 inorganic arsenic 20 for baby food for infants and young children. The toxic inorganic fraction stays infant-capped even though the fish component's TOTAL arsenic is high (organic arsenobetaine); iAs <= tAs holds (20 <= 1000).
iAs.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

tHg.label: government read-across (aquatic) — EU 2023/915 total mercury 500 for muscle meat of fish (general), the fish component's mercury ceiling. PROVISIONAL: pending the Cat-6 species-MeHg read-across decision on whether a fish infant food should carry an infant-protective mercury limit instead.
tHg.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

MeHg.label: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg ≤ tHg). No jurisdiction sets a MeHg limit for this product form below the binding total mercury ceiling (500 µg/kg), so MeHg is governed by and bounded by total mercury; no separate MeHg ceiling is published.

Ni.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2024/1987 nickel 500 for baby food except juices.
Ni.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

Sn.label: government read-across (India FSSAI "Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods" Sn 5000, the only non-canned tin ML in the register) applied at face value.
Sn.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

Al.label: government read-across (AU-NZ Schedule 19 infant-formula Al 500, the only government aluminium ML in any jurisdiction) applied at face value; the 8:1 reconstitution factor is formula-specific and is not applied to a non-formula product.
Al.basis_note: face value (nearest government value; comparator vs any direct limit)

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium ML for any non-dairy infant food; the dairy milk-powder read-across (China 2000) is a weak analogy for a non-dairy matrix. Cr(III) is nutritionally essential and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in-matrix, so total-Cr is not a material toxic in this matrix. Firm control: reflex speciation — any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) speciation by EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + IC-ICP-MS (or equivalent); LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.
Cr.rationale: No government sets a total-chromium ML for any non-dairy infant food; the dairy milk-powder read-across (China 2000) is a weak analogy for a non-dairy matrix. Cr(III) is nutritionally essential and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in-matrix, so total-Cr is not a material toxic in this matrix. Firm control: reflex speciation — any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr.regulatory_basis: No government maximum level for Cr in this product matrix; the toxic species is separately bounded and reflex-speciation-controlled where applicable.
Cr.jurisdictions_checked: EU; UK; CODEX; US; CA; AU-NZ; CN; IN; BR; GSO; KR; EC; MX; TR

Cr-VI.label: Hexavalent chromium is a component of total chromium (Cr-VI ≤ Cr). No jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI limit for this product form below the total chromium determination (reflex speciation: any quantifiable Cr-VI fails), so Cr-VI is governed by and bounded by total chromium; no separate Cr-VI ceiling is published.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, 8:1 basis, read-across)
